description: Documents the conflict-rule families that SHACL cannot express natively, and the SHACL feature gap responsible. The SHACL baseline (shacl_baseline.py) covers the static-constraint subset only.

examples: Record with type=FINANCIAL and PII flag and EU jurisdiction
Matter hold_start..hold_end vs. record validity window
Retention deadline expiry vs. erasure-request timestamp
not_expressible_in_shacl.missing_feature: SHACL has no built-in interval algebra or temporal-relation operators. xsd:dateTime ordering is available only via sh:lessThan / sh:lessThanOrEquals on pairs of properties on the same focus node; multi-node interval relations require SPARQL-based constraints (sh:sparql), which lift the baseline out of 'pure' SHACL and into a SPARQL extension.
not_expressible_in_shacl.spec_reference: SHACL Core 4.6 Property Pair Constraint Components; SHACL-SPARQL 5

examples: SOX vs. SEC: lex-superior, lex-specialis, lex-posterior
Hold vs. erasure: hold prevails as a defeasible default
not_expressible_in_shacl.missing_feature: SHACL evaluates each shape independently; it has no representation of priority among conflicting constraints, no exceptions, and no non-monotonic semantics.
not_expressible_in_shacl.spec_reference: SHACL Core 1 ('SHACL does not provide a built-in mechanism to handle inconsistencies')

not_expressible_in_shacl.missing_feature: SHACL constraints are evaluated per focus node; there is no fixed-point closure operator. Recursion across shapes is explicitly out of scope for SHACL Core and only partially supported via SHACL-SPARQL with implementation-specific semantics.

Could be partially expressed via sh:NodeShape on Matter checking the flags, but the cross-record dependency (record's hold_matters -> matter's exemption flags -> suppression of a conflict on the record) requires either SHACL-SPARQL or post-validation reasoning. Out of scope for pure SHACL Core.

summary: SHACL Core covers the static-constraint surface (per-node type and value constraints). The temporal, defeasible, recursive, and cross-record dimensions that drive T-RKG's incremental value over baselines are out of scope for SHACL Core by construction. A SHACL-SPARQL extension could close part of the gap but is no longer a 'pure' SHACL baseline.
